title: The closure of the diagonal is a common dense refinement
statement:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $f:X\to S$ be separated of finite type, and let
$c_k=(X\xrightarrow{j_k}\overline X_k\xrightarrow{p_k}S)$, $k=1,2$, be
compactifications of $f$. Let $Z$ be the scheme-theoretic image of

$$
\delta=(j_1,j_2):X\longrightarrow P:=\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2 ,
$$

with projections $q_k:Z\to\overline X_k$. Then $\delta$ factors as a
quasi-compact, scheme-theoretically dense open immersion $j:X\to Z$ followed
by the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow P$; the structure map $Z\to S$ is
proper, so $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\to S)$ is a dense compactification; and
each $q_k$ is a refinement $c\to c_k$ in the sense of
[det-nagata-definition-refinement], i.e. $q_kj=j_k$ and
$q_k^{-1}(j_k(X))=j(X)$.

Consequently every finite nonempty family of compactifications of $f$ has a
common dense refinement.

proof.text: Put $P=\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2$. Its first projection is the base change of the proper map $p_2$ along $p_1$, so it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Its composite with $p_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Thus $P\to S$ is proper, in particular separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

For $k\in\{1,2\}$ put $\ell=3-k$ and $P_k^\circ=\mathrm{pr}_k^{-1}(j_k(X))$. The base change of the open immersion $j_k$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $P_k^\circ$ with $X\times_S\overline X_\ell$. In these coordinates $\delta$ is $\Gamma_k=(\mathrm{id}_X,j_\ell)$. The square with top map $\Gamma_k:X\to X\times_S\overline X_\ell$, left map $j_\ell$, bottom map $\Delta_{p_\ell}:\overline X_\ell\to\overline X_\ell\times_S\overline X_\ell$, and right map $(j_\ell\mathrm{pr}_X,\mathrm{pr}_\ell)$ is cartesian: for any test scheme $T$, a map into its pullback is a triple $a:T\to X$, $b:T\to\overline X_\ell$, $c:T\to\overline X_\ell$ satisfying $j_\ell a=c=b$, so is uniquely the triple determined by $a$. Since $p_\ell$ is proper, its diagonal is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] therefore makes each $\Gamma_k$ a closed immersion. In particular $\delta$ factors as $\Gamma_1$ followed by the open immersion $P_1^\circ\to P$, so it is an immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Schemes Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); separatedness is Schemes Definition Tag 01KK, and Morphisms Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion)

proof.text: The input open immersion $j_1$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] in its current form: the composite $p_1j_1=f$ is quasi-compact because $f$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $p_1$ is quasi-separated. Indeed, $p_1$ is proper by [def-nagata-compactification], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse image of any affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence is quasi-compact. Thus [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] applies. Its base change $u:P_1^\circ\to P$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. For each affine open $V\subseteq P$, the open $u^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $\Gamma_1$ is a closed immersion, $\delta^{-1}(V)=\Gamma_1^{-1}(u^{-1}(V))$ is homeomorphic to a closed subspace of $u^{-1}(V)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A closed subspace of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact: adjoin its open complement to any open cover, take a finite subcover, and discard the complement. Thus $\delta$ is quasi-compact, and Step 2 made it an immersion.

source.place: Current blueprint update of lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target (quasi-compact composite and quasi-separated target); Stacks Tags 01K5 and 03GI for base-change and permanence, plus the elementary closed-subspace argument

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] to the quasi-compact immersion $\delta$. It gives the factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{i}P$, with $j$ a quasi-compact, scheme-theoretically dense open immersion. The map $i$ is closed by the definition of the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Since $P\to S$ is proper by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c) makes $Z\to S$ proper. The equations $q_kj=\mathrm{pr}_kij=\mathrm{pr}_k\delta=j_k$ and $p_kq_kj=f$ follow from the projections of the fibre product. Thus these maps give a compactification by [def-nagata-compactification] and a dense one by [def-nagata-dense-compactification].

For $k=1,2$ set $Z_k^\circ=Z\times_P P_k^\circ=q_k^{-1}(j_k(X))$. The closed graph $\Gamma_k:X\to P_k^\circ$ from Step 2 factors through $Z_k^\circ$, because $ij=\delta$. This factor identifies $X$ with a closed subscheme of $Z_k^\circ$: locally, if the two closed subschemes of an affine open of $P_k^\circ$ have ideals $I$ for $Z_k^\circ$ and $J$ for $\Gamma_k$, the factorization says $I\subseteq J$, and the map between them is $A/I\twoheadrightarrow A/J$. This is the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On the other hand $j(X)\subseteq Z_k^\circ$ is open and scheme-theoretically dense: restricting the injection $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_X$ of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open] to $Z_k^\circ$ gives $\mathcal O_{Z_k^\circ}\hookrightarrow (j|_{Z_k^\circ})_*\mathcal O_X$, since $j^{-1}(Z_k^\circ)=X$. The ideal sheaf of the closed copy of $X$ is the kernel of this same map, hence zero. Thus this closed immersion is an isomorphism and $Z_k^\circ=j(X)$ as open subschemes, with their scheme structures. In particular $q_k^{-1}(j_k(X))=j(X)$ for both indices.

source.place: Injectivity criterion in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]; elementary restriction-and-kernel argument for the closed graphs

proof.text: Each $q_k$ is an $S$-morphism, since $p_kq_k$ is the restriction to $Z$ of the structure morphism of $P$. Step 4 gives $q_kj=j_k$ and Step 5 gives the inverse-image identity required in [det-nagata-definition-refinement]. For each input $k$, the open map $j_k$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] in its current form: its composite with the proper map $p_k$ is the finite-type, hence quasi-compact, map $f$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $p_k$ is quasi-separated because [def-nagata-compactification] makes it proper, [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes it separated, and its diagonal has affine inverse images $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], which are quasi-compact, giving [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The new open map is quasi-compact by Step 4. Therefore $q_1,q_2$ are refinements in exactly the stated sense, even if either input compactification has extra components outside $X$.

proof.text: For the finite-family assertion induct on a positive number $n$ of compactifications. For $n=1$, apply Steps 1–6 to $(c_1,c_1)$; this yields a dense compactification refining $c_1$, regardless of whether $c_1$ was dense. If $n>1$ and a dense compactification $d$ refines $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$, apply the pairwise construction already proved in Steps 1–6 to $(d,c_n)$. It yields a dense $e$ with refinements $a:e\to d$ and $b:e\to c_n$. For a previously constructed refinement $r_k:d\to c_k$, the composite $r_ka$ is over $S$, restricts to $j_k$ on $X$, and satisfies $(r_ka)^{-1}(j_k(X))=a^{-1}(j_d(X))=j_e(X)$. These are precisely the composition equations in [det-nagata-definition-refinement]. Thus $e$ refines every member. Enumerating any finite nonempty index set gives the claimed assertion; no empty-family existence assertion is used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_common_dense_refinement {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (c₁ c₂ : Compactification f) : IsClosedImmersion (graph c₁ c₂).imageι ∧ IsOpenImmersion (inf c₁ c₂).i ∧ QuasiCompact (inf c₁ c₂).i ∧ IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant (inf c₁ c₂).i ∧ IsProper (inf c₁ c₂).g ∧ (graph c₁ c₂).toImage ≫ (graph c₁ c₂).imageι = graph c₁ c₂ ∧ (inf c₁ c₂).Z = (graph c₁ c₂).image ∧ (inf c₁ c₂).i = (graph c₁ c₂).toImage ∧ (inf c₁ c₂).g = (graph c₁ c₂).imageι ≫ pullback.fst c₁.g c₂.g ≫ c₁.g ∧ (infFst c₁ c₂).hom = (graph c₁ c₂).imageι ≫ pullback.fst c₁.g c₂.g ∧ (infSnd c₁ c₂).hom = (graph c₁ c₂).imageι ≫ pullback.snd c₁.g c₂.g ∧ Compactification.boundaryRefinementProperty f (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := ⟨inf c₁ c₂, (inf c₁ c₂).quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) (Y := ⟨c₁, c₁.quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) ⟨(infFst c₁ c₂).hom, (infFst c₁ c₂).i_hom, (infFst c₁ c₂).hom_g⟩) ∧ Compactification.boundaryRefinementProperty f (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := ⟨inf c₁ c₂, (inf c₁ c₂).quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) (Y := ⟨c₂, c₂.quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) ⟨(infSnd c₁ c₂).hom, (infSnd c₁ c₂).i_hom, (infSnd c₁ c₂).hom_g⟩) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) [Finite I] [Nonempty I] (d : I → Compactification f), ∃ (e : Compactification f), IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant e.i ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ (h : e.Z ⟶ (d i).Z), ∃ (hj : e.i ≫ h = (d i).i), ∃ (hS : h ≫ (d i).g = e.g), Compactification.boundaryRefinementProperty f (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := ⟨e, e.quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) (Y := ⟨d i, (d i).quasiCompact_openImmersion inferInstance⟩) ⟨h, hj, hS⟩))
